sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Pinned list of libraries
sections.what: Names each library the OCR service needs with its exact version, from the web framework to image and PDF tools.
sections.why: Keeps every install identical so tests and production behave the same.
sections.watch_out: Changing one version can break others, so run the tests after any change.

summary: Lists the Python libraries the OCR service needs, each pinned to one exact version.
purpose: Tells the installer which libraries to download so the OCR service behaves the same on every machine.
why: Pinned versions prevent surprise breakage when a library publishes a new release.
how: Each line names a library and an exact version. pip reads the list and installs each one, including large libraries such as opencv and spacy.
inputs: Read by pip during CI and during the Docker build.
outputs: An installed set of libraries for the OCR service.
risks: Several listed libraries (PyPDF2, pdfplumber, spacy, redis, boto3, httpx, structlog) do not appear in the code shown, so they may be unused. Tesseract, the text-reading program, is not listed and must be installed separately. pytest is not listed; CI installs it separately.
debug: If an install fails, confirm the pinned version exists for the Python version used in CI, which is 3.11. If OCR returns nothing, confirm Tesseract is installed on the machine.
